Compute the metrics of several fitted models

Source: R/evaluation.R
evaluate_insample.Rd

Runs model_metrics() on each fit in a list and binds the rows, with a model column and a metric_basis column saying whether each row is in-sample, out-of-bag or on newdata. It takes a single spatial_fit too. No model is refitted: the fitted values are read with fitted(), and newdata is scored with predict(). compare_models() adds information criteria and residual Moran's I to the same table.

Usage

evaluate_insample(fits, newdata = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fits

A spatial_fit object, or a named list of them (e.g. list(GWR = gwr_obj, Bayesian = bayes_obj)). The names are used as the model labels and every element must have one; an unnamed list is an error, and so are duplicated names. model is the key the comparison table is assembled on, so two fits sharing a name cannot be told apart in the output.

newdata

Optional sf object for out-of-sample evaluation. Must contain the response variable and all predictors. If NULL, in-sample metrics are computed.

...

Passed to predict() when newdata is given. Without newdata nothing reads them, so any argument here is an error, which catches a misspelt newdata.

Value

A data.frame with one row per model and columns for model name, all regression metrics, and metric_basis: what the row's metrics were computed on, "in-sample" (fitted values), "out-of-bag" (an rf_fit's fitted values, see "What the metrics are computed on") or "newdata". Rows with different bases do not compare like for like. An element that is not a spatial_fit is skipped, with a logged warning, and has no row; a list in which no element is a spatial_fit is an error.

Details

The metrics are those of model_metrics(): see its sections "What the metrics are computed on" and "Percentage errors on responses with zeros".

See also

Other in-sample checks: compare_models(), model_metrics(), print.morans_i(), residual_morans_i()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
pts <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(60, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(60, 0, 1000),
             a = rnorm(60)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
# An offset keeps the response away from zero, where MAPE is undefined.
pts$z <- 10 + 2 * pts$a + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3)
# Fit on 40 rows and keep 20 back, so the second call is out of sample.
fit <- fit_rf_model(pts[1:40, ], "z", "a", num_trees = 50, seed = 1)
evaluate_insample(fit)                           # out-of-bag for a forest
#>    model  n     RMSE       MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_MAPE
#> 1 rf_fit 40 0.409009 0.3236812 3.425689 3.390414 0.9541711     NA     40
#>   n_SMAPE metric_basis
#> 1      40   out-of-bag
evaluate_insample(fit, newdata = pts[41:60, ])   # on the 20 held-out rows
#>    model  n      RMSE       MAE    MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_MAPE
#> 1 rf_fit 20 0.5080838 0.3836504 3.56621 3.649174 0.9022065     NA     20
#>   n_SMAPE metric_basis
#> 1      20      newdata
